candidates.label: Smyrna (Roman-era city, İzmir)
candidates.support: This is the Roman-period city addressed in Revelation, at the location of modern İzmir's ancient agora, distinct from the earlier 'Old Smyrna' settlement at nearby Bayraklı; the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's coordinate for the site and Wikidata's coordinate agree closely.

summary.text: Smyrna was an old Greek city on the Aegean coast, destroyed by the Lydian king Alyattes around 600 BC; its people then lived scattered in villages until the Hellenistic kings Antigonus and Lysimachus gathered them into a new city around 290 BC, on the slopes of Mount Pagos above a closable harbor. According to the Greek geographer Strabo, the new city was laid out with an unusually good plan of straight, stone-paved streets; its lower town held large public porticoes, a library, and a shrine to the Greek poet Homer, whom the Smyrnaeans claimed as their own. In AD 26, Smyrna won a contest before the Roman Senate against the rival city of Sardis for the right to build a temple to the emperor Tiberius, on the strength of its long loyalty to Rome.

history.text: Smyrna is one of the seven churches addressed in Revelation 2-3. Unlike most of the other churches, it receives no rebuke: the risen Christ tells the congregation, "I know your works, oppression, and your poverty (but you are rich)," and the text describes local opponents in harsh terms, as "those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan." The letter promises that those faithful even to death will receive "the crown of life," a phrase some interpreters connect to "the crown of Smyrna," a local expression for the ring of splendid public buildings crowning the hill above the city.
Later, the Christian leader Polycarp was burned to death in the city's stadium during public games held there. The city was afterwards struck by a disastrous earthquake and restored.
Today Smyrna survives as İzmir, a major city on Türkiye's Aegean coast, built over the ancient site.

scripture.textWEB: saying, “What you see, write in a book and send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.”
“To the angel of the assembly in Smyrna write: “The first and the last, who was dead, and has come to life says these things:
“I know your works, oppression, and your poverty (but you are rich), and the blasphemy of those who say they are Jews, and they are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.

Don’t be afraid of the things which you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to throw some of you into prison, that you may be tested; and you will have oppression for ten days. Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
